author: Petra Stock
description:
The $134,000 cost of the statue of the former Victorian premier has been heavily criticised by the Liberal opposition

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The Carroll government in Victoria has cancelled controversial plans for a statue of former Labor premier Daniel Andrews.

Work began in May on the statue commemorating the former premier’s more than 3,000 days in office, as part of a 1999 policy recognising long-serving Victorian premiers.

Continue reading...
title: Controversial plans for a Daniel Andrews sculpture officially scrapped by Victorian government

author: Nadeem Badshah
description:
Six more people hospitalised after incident at Big Church festival near Steyning

A 41-year-old man has died and at least six other people have been injured after a large sign fell at a Christian festival in West Sussex, police said.

The man, from Eastbourne, East Sussex, was pronounced dead at the scene after the incident at the Big Church festival off Washington Road near Steyning on Friday afternoon.

Continue reading...
title: Man, 41, dies after large sign falls at Christian festival in West Sussex

author: Cait Kelly in Kathmandu
description:
The figure rose to 41 on Saturday morning, with four rapid response teams to arrive in Kathmandu

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The number of Australians who were reported missing in the catastrophic Nepal flooding disaster has risen to 41, as one family celebrates after an unaccounted-for woman made contact with them yesterday.

It means three additional Australians were confirmed missing overnight – up from 38 who remained unaccounted for on Friday evening.

Continue reading...
title: Number of Australians missing in Nepal’s deadly floods rises again, as Albanese deploys more personnel

author: Gabrielle Canon
description:
Nearly 600 days after the devastating 2025 fires, thousands of Los Angeles residents are still waiting for more than $15bn in federal funds to rebuild their communities

As thousands of residents in Spokane, Washington, begin to grapple with a long recovery after a destructive set of blazes that consumed hundreds of homes in the state’s second most populated city this month, victims of the Los Angeles firestorm broke a grim record – they have faced the longest delay in modern history for federal aid.

Nearly 600 days since a historic firestorm roared into communities across Los Angeles, reducing more than 16,000 structures to ash and toxic debris, the Trump administration has failed to appropriate more than $15bn in long-term recovery funds that are crucial to rebuilding. The delay in supplying the badly needed funds is months longer
title: Los Angeles fire survivors face record wait for federal disaster aid under Trump

author: Associated Press
description:
National Park Service, which backs the 250ft arch, says it is likely to disrupt historical significance of dozens of sites

A new National Park Service report backs Donald Trump’s proposed arch, despite what it says are adverse effects to the sightlines of a host of landmarks in Washington, including the Washington Monument and the Lincoln and Jefferson memorials.

The report released on Friday says the 250ft-tall (76-meter) memorial arch is likely to disrupt the historical significance of dozens of sites near its planned location adjacent to the Arlington Memorial Bridge.

Continue reading...
title: Trump arch will alter sightlines of many Washington DC landmarks, report says

author: Uwa Ede-Osifo
description:
Climber, stuck on 6in ridge, had veered off treacherous path and ‘any fall would almost certainly be fatal’

An ill-fated move left a man stranded on a 6in ledge over 10,000ft off the ground for hours in California’s Sierra Nevada mountain range, before a volunteer rescue team came to his aid.

The climber, who has not been publicly identified, had been scaling the Mendenhall couloir, a gully on the face of Laurel mountain, with a friend on Saturday.

Continue reading...
title: Volunteers rescue man stuck on 10,000ft-high ledge in Sierra Nevada

author: Guardian staff
description:
A former editor of Breitbart News, Yiannopoulos has also served as an intern for Marjorie Taylor Greene

Milo Yiannopoulos, a far-right British political commentator, was detained by Immigration and Customs Enforcement in Louisiana, according to the Department of Homeland Security (DHS).

In a statement on Friday, a DHS spokesperson said that Yiannopoulos was arrested on Thursday at the Louis Armstrong New Orleans international airport (MSY). The spokesperson said Yiannopoulos “legally entered the country” in May 2019, but that “he chose to overstay his welcome in violation of our nation’s laws”.

Continue reading...
title: Milo Yiannopoulos, a far-right political commentator, reportedly detained by ICE

author: Press Association
description:
Cleveland police say a total of 24 people arrested in investigation after crash that killed two officers

Seven more men have been arrested as Cleveland police attempt to disrupt organised crime after the A66 crash that killed two officers.

The force said the total number of those arrested in the investigation had risen to 24, several of them charged with serious offences and a number of offenders recalled to prison.

Continue reading...
title: Police arrest seven more men in aftermath of deadly A66 crash

author: Guardian staff and agencies
description:
About 125 firefighters tackle blaze at Neasden waste facility as nearby Amazon warehouse is evacuated

A large fire has broken out at a waste facility close to Wembley Stadium in north-west London, disrupting tube and train lines in the area.

Twenty fire engines and about 125 firefighters were sent to tackle the blaze at a mixed-waste facility on an industrial estate in Neasden, just under a mile from the venue.

Continue reading...
title: Large fire near Wembley Stadium disrupts tube and rail services

author: Dani Anguiano
description:
Nevada-based Kingsbarn Realty Capital seeks to acquire land to construct private road to development outside park

The Trump administration is reportedly pushing to give a parcel of land inside Yosemite, the country’s first national park and one of its most popular, to a Nevada-based private developer.

Staff with the National Park Service have been exploring how the agency can give a quarter-mile parcel to a company operated by Kingsbarn Realty Capital, the news outlet Notus reported on Friday, citing agency documents and unnamed sources “directly familiar with discussions”.

Continue reading...
title: Trump administration pushing to hand parcel of Yosemite land to private developer – report

author: Maya Yang and agency
description:
Official death toll approaches 600, with many of the missing Americans having been on a pilgrimage to a sacred site

At least 90 Americans were still missing on Friday among almost 2,000 people unaccounted for following the catastrophic flash flood along the Nepal-Tibet border on Wednesday.

With the official death toll creeping towards 600 on Friday and expected to continue rising, there were survivors, victims and missing people from many nationalities.

Continue reading...
title: At least 90 Americans missing in Nepal flood among 2,000 unaccounted for

author: Peter Walker Senior political correspondent
description:
Moscow recruiting an estimated 1,000 people a day, but officials say it cannot keep up with its level of casualties

Russia is losing about 6,000 more troops in Ukraine each month than it can recruit, western officials have said.

While Russia is still acquiring new battlefield recruits at speed, with an estimated rate of 1,000 a day, in the last two months even this has not been sufficient to replace those killed or injured.

Continue reading...
title: Russia losing 6,000 more troops than it can recruit each month in Ukraine, says west

author: Andrew Gregory Health editor in Munich
description:
New guidance by world’s top cardiovascular health groups upgrades types of attacks that primarily affect women

Doctors have agreed the world’s first universal definition of a heart attack, paving the way for millions of women to finally receive better treatment after decades of being “deprioritised”.

In one of the biggest procedural shakeups in a generation, the world’s four leading cardiovascular health groups have signed off on new guidance for healthcare professionals when seeing suspected heart attack patients.

Continue reading...
title: Doctors promise care ‘revolution’ as they agree first universal definition of heart attack

author: Pippa Neill Environment reporter
description:
Campaigners say ‘seismic shift’ follows years of pressure to sever ties with oil and gas firm

The London Science Museum has ended its decades-long partnership with the oil and gas company BP in what has been described as a “seismic shift” for the museum.

The Science Museum Group academy, which was established in 2018 to provide training and resources, announced on Friday that it would be ending its partnership with BP. In a statement, the director and chief executive of the Science Museum Group, Sir Ian Blatchford, said the partnership had “drawn to a close at the end of the current contract term”.

Continue reading...
title: London Science Museum cuts links with BP after decades of partnership

author: Tobi Thomas Health and inequalities correspondent
description:
Experts say imported eggs served in cafes and restaurants may be behind hundreds of infections and one death

Salmonella cases in the UK are expected to rise until the common source is identified, something that is notoriously difficult to establish, experts have warned.

There have been 474 confirmed cases and one death linked to the current outbreak, according to the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA), with the latest investigations suggesting it is associated with eating imported eggs in cafes and restaurants.

Continue reading...
title: Salmonella cases in UK likely to rise until source of outbreak is found

author: Hannah Ellis-Petersen in Bidur, Sam Jones and agencies
description:
Federation says it fears death toll of more than 540 will continue to rise as rescuers reach cut-off areas

  • Nepal-Tibet flash flood – latest updates

  • Visual guide: how the deadly flooding unfolded

  • Tell us: have you been affected by the flash floods?

The Red Cross has said at least 93,000 people may have been affected by Wednesday’s flash floods on the Nepal-Tibet border, which have killed more than 540 people, left another 1,900 missing, and triggered a huge rescue operation that is being hampered by fears o
title: At least 93,000 ‘in great need’ after Nepal-Tibet flash floods, says Red Cross

author: Gaya Gupta
description:
However, Kevin Warsh didn’t say if interest rates would change in coming months, as inflation remains stubborn

The US Federal Reserve is not done fighting high inflation, its chair, Kevin Warsh, said in his first major speech in the role on Friday, emphasizing that it is “the Fed’s job to deliver stable prices”.

Warsh did not indicate where the Fed will take interest rates in the coming months, despite US inflation remaining stubbornly above the central bank’s 2% target amid the war in Iran. But his speech was taken by markets as a signal that rates may rise in the coming months, a move that may put him at odds with Donald Trump, who has aggressively called for rates to be cut.

Continue reading...
title: Fed chair addresses inflation and says central bank’s job is ‘to deliver stable prices’

author: Associated Press
description:
Officials said Tyrin Johnson turned toward guard members with gun while running as report shows he was shot in back

Tennessee national guard members assigned to a federal anti-crime taskforce in Memphis fatally shot an armed 20-year-old man in the back, according to an autopsy report obtained by the Associated Press, contradicting police accounts that said the man was facing the troops when they fired.

Authorities have said that Tyrin Johnson turned toward guard members with a gun while running from them in the early morning hours after the Fourth of July holiday in Memphis when he was fatally shot in the chest.

Continue reading...
title: Tennessee national guard fatally shot armed man in back, autopsy shows

author: Shrai Popat in Washington
description:
President faces criticism over plan to import up to 300,000 metric tons of foreign beef without charging higher tariffs

Donald Trump has pledged to allow cattle ranchers and farmers to process their own food amid a backlash from the US agricultural sector over his decision to pause US tariffs on foreign beef.

The US president has been sharply criticized, including from members of his own party, since announcing the US will temporarily import up to 300,000 metric tons of foreign beef without charging higher tariffs in a bid to bring down prices.

Continue reading...
title: Trump pledges to allow cattle ranchers to process own food amid beef imports backlash

author: Anna Betts
description:
Weather system is forecast to approach the Leeward Islands this weekend and may produce flash flooding

Tropical Storm Dolly is moving quickly across the Atlantic Ocean toward the Leeward Islands and is expected to bring significant rainfall to parts of the Caribbean this weekend, the National Hurricane Center (NHC) said on Friday morning.

Dolly, which formed on Thursday, had maximum sustained winds of near 40mph (65km/h) with higher gusts as of Friday.

Continue reading...
title: Tropical Storm Dolly speeding across Atlantic toward the Caribbean

author: Richard Luscombe
description:
State to offer up to 5,000 trappers chance to snare reptiles whose numbers have risen to 3m from fewer than 100,000

The first recreational alligator hunt in Louisiana in more than half a century is about to commence in the swamps of that state, with up to 5,000 hopeful trappers facing strict rules in order to snare a reptile.

The state’s fish and wildlife commission banned alligator hunting in 1962 to allow the species to recover after decades of unregulated killings for meat and hides dropped numbers there to below 100,000.

Continue reading...
title: Louisiana gears up for first recreational alligator hunt in more than 50 years

author: Fiona Harvey Environment editor
description:
Brazil has failed to prove compliance with EU rules on use of antibiotics in cattle and poultry farming

The UK’s leading farming organisations and animal health experts have called for an urgent ban on imports of Brazilian meat, in light of concerns over the safety of imports.

The National Farmers’ Union in England and its sister organisations in the devolved administrations wrote to the government on Friday warning that public health was at risk.

Continue reading...
title: UK urged to ban imports of Brazilian meat over health concerns

author: Robert Booth UK technology editor
description:
Government says Green leader’s proposed moratorium on ‘energy-guzzling’ AI projects would be disaster for economy

Labour has rejected calls to pause construction of major AI infrastructure in Britain after the Green party leader, Zack Polanski, said it was time to “slam the brakes on these energy-guzzling, water-guzzling datacentres”.

The government hit back at the opposition party’s proposal of a “moratorium other than [for] local-scale datacentres for the local community”, saying it “would be a disaster for jobs and national security”.

Continue reading...
title: Labour rejects Zack Polanski’s call to ‘slam brakes’ on building AI datacentres

author: Anne Davies
description:
The brother of former premier questioned over what, if anything, was done in return for $2m from developer turned fugitive Jean Nassif

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Finally, we are hearing from one of the central characters, Charles Perrottet, in a saga that has occupied the Independent Commission against Corruption (Icac) for nearly four years.

It began with the dismissal of the Hills Shire council and a late night 2022 speech in NSW parliament alleging secret payments from a developer. It pirouetted to a pressure campaign allegedly to remove the then NSW building commissioner, and ended with real world impacts: defective high-rise buildings and thousands of unhappy homebuyers, with the developer nowhere to be see
title: Charles Perrottet becomes Icac’s main character amid claims of hidden payments and political hit jobs

author: Peter Walker Senior political correspondent
description:
Exclusive: PM also warns his ministers against trying to influence vote when bill returns to Commons next month

Andy Burnham has told Labour MPs that he will not cast a vote when the assisted dying bill returns to the Commons next month to avoid influencing the debate.

While the move was welcomed by supporters of the measure, No 10 officials say the prime minister has no wish to affect the process in either direction, and is just doing what he thinks is best to allow MPs to reach their own collective view.

Continue reading...
title: Andy Burnham to abstain on assisted dying bill to avoid influencing debate

author: Jamie Grierson
description:
Critics say painting looks more like a zombie but artist Chris Ashmore says ‘touch-ups’ are still to happen

A street artist has defended his mural of snooker player Ronnie O’Sullivan in Sheffield after critics suggested the world champion looks like a zombie.

Chris Ashmore was commissioned to produce the artwork featuring the seven-time world champion for the back wall of the Spot On Snooker Club, the BBC reported.

Continue reading...
title: Artist defends Ronnie O’Sullivan mural in Sheffield saying it isn’t finished

author: Deborah Cole in Berlin
description:
Police hunt two suspects after historic 200-carat piece is snatched from Austrian museum during opening hours

Austrian police are hunting two men alleged to have stolen a 200-carat platinum necklace encrusted with 673 diamonds that was on loan to a museum in Vienna and once belonged to Egyptian royalty.

Authorities in the capital released pictures of the suspects captured by security cameras during the heist at the Museum of Applied Arts (MAK), amid a rash of spectacular smash-and-grab thefts from European cultural institutions.

Continue reading...
title: Egyptian queen’s 673-diamond necklace stolen in Vienna smash-and-grab raid

author: Amy Hawkins Senior China correspondent
description:
Scale of devastation emerges in Nepal as reporters reach disaster area, but Chinese state media focus more on rescue efforts

  • Nepal-Tibet flash flood – latest updates

In the days since an enormous glacier in the Himalayas snapped away from a mountaintop and cascaded into the valley below, the true scale of the devastation caused by the flash floods in Nepal and Tibet is still unfolding.

But the picture is emerging far more quickly in Nepal than in China, where strict controls on the flow of information from one of its most sensitive regions are hampering the public’s understanding of events.
title: Chinese control of information hampers assessment of Tibet flood damage

author: Uwa Ede-Osifo
description:
X2 ride at Magic Mountain has been closed for a month after one rider experienced brain compression and another remains in coma

An infamous Six Flags Magic Mountain rollercoaster, long favored by intrepid theme park goers, has been closed for more than a month after two people say they experienced brain injuries after riding it, according to a new CNN investigation.

The X2 rollercoaster can send riders plummeting and twisting hundreds of feet, reaching up to 76mph (about 122km/h), as the seats rotate 360 degrees. On the southern California theme park’s website, it’s advertised as a rite of passage for daredevils.

Continue reading...
title: Rollercoaster at LA’s Six Flags shut after two riders suffered brain injuries, inquiry finds

author: Richard Luscombe and agency
description:
Helipad relocation led in part to incident where Marine One, carrying the president, had close call with passenger jet

Safety officials say the relocation of a helipad amid Donald Trump’s multi-project White House reconstruction led in part to an incident earlier this month in which a military helicopter carrying the president came too close to a passenger jet.

A preliminary report published Thursday by the National Transportation ⁠Safety Board (NTSB) blamed “communication issues” for the failure of the crew of Marine One, the presidential helicopter, to give the required three minutes’ notice to air traffic controllers that they were about to take off from the White House.

Continue reading...
title: White House construction played part in Trump helicopter incident, safety officials say

author: Angelique Chrisafis in Paris
description:
Speech part of effort to strengthen National Rally party’s international ties before Marine Le Pen’s presidential bid

The French far-right leader Jordan Bardella is to give a speech at Reform UK’s party conference in Birmingham next week as he attempts to boost international ties before Marine Le Pen’s bid for the French presidency next spring.

Le Pen’s far-right, anti-immigration National Rally (RN) is high in the polls and she is predicted to reach the final round of the French presidential race in May.

Continue reading...
title: French far-right leader Jordan Bardella to address Reform UK party conference

author: Melody Schreiber
description:
Anti-vaxxers are spreading conspiracy theories after two recent measles-associated deaths in Pennsylvania

Anti-vaccine activists are trying to track down the families of two people, including at least one newborn, who died after contracting measles in Pennsylvania, as governor Josh Shapiro tangles with Robert F Kennedy Jr over his “inaccurate and misleading claims”.

Kennedy, the secretary of the US Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), suggested late Wednesday that the deaths in the state may have been “fabricated” after a Republican coroner – an elected political office in Lancaster county – claimed one of the measles-associated deaths was unrelated to the virus, although the given cause would be consistent with measles.

Continue reading...
title: Vaccine misinformation spreads as RFK Jr suggests two measles deaths were ‘fabricated’

author: Rachel Hall
description:
Desperate relatives trying to reach loved ones last seen in area where entire villages have been swept away

  • Nepal-Tibet flash flood – latest updates

  • Visual guide: how the deadly flooding unfolded

  • Tell us: have you been affected by the flash floods?

Families are rushing to Nepal to search for the 33 British nationals who are still missing, as fears mount over the risk of a second wave of flooding in the region.
title: Families of 33 missing Britons rush to Nepal as fears grow of more floods

author: Sian Cain
description:
Jake says his parents ‘never stopped helping’ his brother Nick, who has pleaded not guilty to murdering both of them at their Los Angeles home

Jake Reiner has given his first interview since the killing of his parents, the film-maker Rob Reiner and his wife, Michele Singer Reiner, saying: “I will never understand why this happened.”

Reiner, who directed films including The Princess Bride, This is Spinal Tap and Stand By Me, was found dead alongside Singer Reiner from apparent stab wounds in their home in Los Angeles in December.

Continue reading...
title: Rob Reiner’s son Jake gives first interview after parents’ deaths: ‘I will never understand why this happened’

author: Sarah Butler
description:
Chair Allan Leighton says lower prices and an improved online service are attracting more shoppers

Asda has heralded its first quarterly growth in more than two years as the supermarket’s boss said it was attracting more shoppers with lower prices and an improved online service.

Allan Leighton, the executive chair of the UK’s third-largest grocer, said a 0.2% rise in sales at established stores, excluding fuel, in the three months to the end of June was “a huge milestone” which was “psychologically important for the business”. In the previous quarter sales had fallen 2.3%.

Continue reading...
title: Asda returns to growth after more than two years

author: Michael Savage Media editor
description:
Christian Drogan’s Invading Britain shows former builder turned journalist trying to travel from France to England in small boat

Rupert Murdoch’s online channel TalkTV is facing criticism after it did not disclose that a journalist who travelled to Britain in a small boat for a documentary was a Reform party member and activist.

The channel revealed the “world exclusive” this week, stating that the treacherous journey had made the former builder turned journalist Christian Drogan the first British man “to invade his own country”.

Continue reading...
title: TalkTV under fire for not disclosing reporter’s ties to Reform UK in Channel crossing film

author: Vivian Ho
description:
More than 1,300 people are missing in Nepal and in Tibet after catastrophic flash floods swept through the region, killing at least 469. Plus: Six months of the war in Iran

  • Don’t already get First Thing in your inbox? Sign up here

Good morning.

Rescue operations have resumed in Nepal and Tibet after a pause when a lake at the border began to overflow. The lake was formed when a wall of mud and debris hit the hub of Gyirong in Tibet on Wednesday, causing catastrophic flash floods that thundered down valleys and obliterated villages.

What could have caused this deadly flash flood
title: First Thing: Rescue efforts continue as death toll rises in Nepal-Tibet flood

author: Maya Yang
description:
Decision to rescind ‘roadless rule’ opens more than 45m acres of national forests to roads, drilling and logging

More than 400 endangered animal and plant species could face accelerated extinction after the Donald Trump administration’s decision to rescind a rule that has protected old-growth forests for more than two decades.

According to a new report from the Center for Biological Diversity, the rollback of the Bill Clinton-era “roadless rule” could put 7.4m acres of endangered-species habitat and nearly 1
title: Trump rollback of US forest protections could accelerate extinction of 400 endangered species

author: Lauren Almeida
description:
Average cost of petrol reaches 161.6p a litre, while diesel costs average of 183.4p, according to the AA

UK petrol prices have hit their highest level since 2022, piling more financial pressure on motorists before the bank holiday weekend.

The average cost of petrol has reached 161.6p a litre, while diesel costs an average of 183.4p a litre, according to the breakdown company the AA.

Continue reading...
title: UK petrol prices hit highest level in almost four years as bank holiday getaway looms

author: Tom Ambrose
description:
Judge Indira Talwani placed a 14-day hold on government implementing Trump’s order to limit mail voting

  • Sign up for the US Breaking News email

Donald Trump’s administration is facing calls to launch an investigation into allegations that Michael Boren, a senior official who oversees the US Forest Service, pressed agency staff to deploy additional resources to fight a fire burning near his Idaho ranch.

Three Democratic senators accused Boren of “inappropriate interference” in a letter seen by the Guardian, demanding answers from Brooke Rollins, US agricultural s
title: Swift appeal likely as judge blocks Trump mail voting order – US politics live

author: Sarah Butler
description:
Sales of beans, lentils and soya bean derivatives on rise while Britons buy less real and fake meat

British shoppers are munching more beans, lentils, tofu and tempeh – while cutting back on real and plant-based fake meat – to save money and improve their diet.

The amount of beans, pulses and soya bean derivatives sold in the UK increased by 7.3% in the first half of 2026 compared with the same period last year, led by a rise in cheap dried lentils, an analysis has found.

Continue reading...
title: Jumping beans: UK shoppers turn to legumes to save cash and improve diet

author: Ramon Antonio Vargas and David Hammer of WWL Louisiana in New Orleans
description:
Survivors begin receiving letters with payment amounts months after $305m settlement agreement was struck

Survivors of child rape and other sexual abuse within New Orleans’s Roman Catholic archdiocese learned that $641,000 or so is the most they can individually get under a settlement approved in December to resolve a years-long bankruptcy protection case.

Those amounts were communicated in letters that hundreds of clergy abuse survivors participating in the New Orleans archdiocese’s bankruptcy began quietly receiving on Tuesday. The figures are well below a $2.4m jury verdict awarded to an unrelated Louisiana religious sexual abuse claimant in June 2025 after the state’s legislature temporarily eliminated filing deadlines for such cases.
title: ‘This whole thing’s a farce’: New Orleans Catholic church sex abuse settlement brings anger and shock

author: Heather Stewart and Lauren Almeida
description:
Chancellor pledges ‘fiscal discipline’ as plan to spend 3% of GDP on defence by 2030 deferred until 2027 review

The new chancellor, John Healey, will delay setting out when the UK will meet the target of spending 3% of GDP on defence until next year’s spending review, the Treasury has confirmed.

Healey resigned as defence secretary in June under Keir Starmer’s leadership, accusing the then prime minister of being “unable” and the Treasury “unwilling” to “commit the resources that the nation needs to defend the country”.

Continue reading...
title: John Healey to duck meeting UK defence spending target in budget

author: Jamie Grierson
description:
Soaring demand for services has led to tenfold increase in spending in a year in some areas, says NHS Alliance

NHS leaders have warned that the costs of meeting soaring demand for attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and autism services in England are “running out of control” and have become unsustainable, with spending in some areas rising by as much as tenfold over the course of a year.

The NHS Alliance, which represents health managers, said the rise in demand since the coronavirus pandemic was forcing some to close waiting lists and look at reining in other services they provide.

Continue reading...
title: ADHD and autism costs in England ‘running out of control’, NHS leaders warn

author: Australian Associated Press
description:
Two 17-year-olds accused of subjecting teenage girl to hours-long sexual assault granted bail

Two boys allegedly invited to join a “degrading” and “humiliating” gang rape in Sydney have been granted bail.

The pair are among three-17-year-olds accused of subjecting a teenage girl to an hours-long sexual assault on the night of 16 August.

Continue reading...
title: Teen boy allegedly messaged two others to join ‘degrading’ and ‘humiliating’ Sydney gang rape, court hears

author: Nino Bucci
description:
Cara Severino has spoken with her parents – but still faces a trek of more than 110km to reach Kathmandu on foot

  • ‘So desperately loved’: ADF member among dozens of Australians missing in Nepal floods as families pray for safe return

  • How Nepali diaspora is responding to flood disaster and how Australians can help in relief effort

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

An Australian woman has made contact with her family, more than two days after she was reported mis
title: ‘We praise God’: Australian woman feared missing in Nepal flooding makes contact with family

author: Brendan Wood and Faye Hulton for MetDesk
description:
Flash flooding and mudslides in Ishikawa and Toyama prefectures, while convective storms hit western Europe

After an “unprecedented” deluge in Chiba in mid-August, Japan has experienced further extreme rainfall in recent days. Moisture from the Sea of Japan brought relentless heavy rain to the prefectures of Ishikawa and Toyama on Thursday.

In Himi, Toyama, 361.5mm of rain fell in 24 hours, equivalent to half the average annual rainfall in London and Paris. Several rivers burst their banks, triggering flash floods and mudslides, felling and damaging buildings.

Continue reading...
title: Weather tracker: More extreme rain in Japan and a tornado in France

author: Jon Henley Europe correspondent
description:
Crown Prince Haakon’s wife, Mette-Marit, corresponded with late US sex offender between 2011 and 2014, long after he was convicted

King Harald V of Norway has died at the age of 89, the palace in Oslo has announced, triggering the succession of his son, Haakon, whose wife Mette-Marit’s association with Jeffrey Epstein has sparked fierce recent controversy.

“It is with deep sadness that we announce that His Majesty King Harald passed away today. King Harald passed away peacefully at Oslo University Hospital on Friday, August 28 at 6.35 am,” the palace said in a statement.

Continue reading...
title: Norway’s King Harald dies leaving stormy succession over crown princess’s Epstein links

author: Penry Buckley
description:
Brother of former state premier sent message to wife regarding apparent plan to damage career of rival

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Charles Perrottet wrote about a plan to damage a Liberal minister’s career following his brother’s accession to the New South Wales premiership in October 2021, stating “we execute the prick once party room is over”, a corruption inquiry has heard.

Anita Perrottet told the Independent Commission Against Corruption (Icac) on
title: ‘We execute the prick’: Charles Perrottet plotted political downfall of NSW Liberal minister, Icac hears

author: Staff and agencies
description:
Lake has formed at epicentre of flood, forcing rescue teams to withdraw, Chinese state media report

  • Nepal flash flood – latest updates

  • Nearly 1,400 missing, mostly tourists, and hundreds killed

  • Visual guide: how the deadly flooding unfolded

  • Tell us: have you been affected by the flash floods?<
title: Flood risk forces halt to rescues in Tibet, as Nepal death toll rises to 469

author: Lisa Cox
description:
Australian government announces 24 expeditioners based at research station on Macquarie Island will be evacuated over possible ‘prolonged psychological stress’

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A dolphin has died from H5 bird flu in South Australia, marking the second native mammal species known to have contracted the virus.

It comes as the federal government announced it would withdraw researchers from the sub-Antarctic Macquarie Island research station due to the “psychosocial risk” of witnessing potential mass seal deaths from H5N1 during the upcoming seal breeding season.
title: Dolphin dies from H5 bird flu in SA as researchers withdrawn from sub-Antarctic island over ‘psychosocial risk’

author: Adeshola Ore Community affairs reporter
description:
Nepali and Tibetan communities plan vigils and work to raise funds for recovery in ‘devastating’ time

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Australia’s Nepali community plan to host vigils to remember the victims of the Nepal-Tibet flood disaster to coincide with a day of mourning, as the number of people killed continues to rise.

As Australia’s Nepali diaspora wait for the full scale of the disaster to become clear, community members are desperately waiting to hear from missing relatives and friends.

Nepal police said on Friday that the death toll had risen to 469, with more than 1,300 people still missing, after massive flash floods and landslides tore through the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli river basins on Thursday
title: How Nepali diaspora is responding to flood disaster and how Australians can help in relief effort

author: Jordyn Beazley
description:
Book was removed for review earlier this month following complaint but reinstated after petition and State Library letter to Waverley council

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A Sydney library has returned to its borrowing shelves a book critical of Israel called How to Sell a Genocide following a public campaign and an intervention from the State Library of New South Wales.

Waverley library
title: Bondi library returns book How to Sell a Genocide to shelves after State Library ‘outlines the law’

author: Australian Associated Press
description:
Coronor finds 31-year-old deviated from a walking track as dusk fell, four days before the winter solstice

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Overlapping errors, including a lack of preparation in near-freezing winter weather, contributed to the death of a Belgian tourist on a wilderness track.

Celine Cremer set off on a walk at Philosopher Falls in Tasmania’s remote north-west on 17 June 2023 and was reported missing almost 10 days later.
title: ‘Confluence of errors’ led to Belgian tourist Celine Cremer’s death in Tasmanian wilderness, coroner finds

author: Andrew Messenger
description:
Man – referred to as MM by court – will keep his identity hidden after legal challenge against suppression dismissed

The identity of a high-profile Queensland man drawn into a Cairns extortion case will remain secret, after the state’s supreme court threw out a legal challenge against a suppression order.

The man – referred to as MM by the court – was drawn into an extortion case earlier this year. He is not a party to the case and is not accused of any offence.

Continue reading...
title: Identity of high-profile Queensland man drawn into extortion case to remain secret after court ruling

author: Australian Associated Press
description:
Barrister for former St Kilda player says he will appeal both the sentence and the conviction for unprovoked assault in May 2025

Former AFL star Nicky Winmar has been jailed for six months for attacking a woman in a violent assault.

Winmar, 60, dropped his head as he was sentenced in Bendigo magistrates court over the May 2025 assault against a woman at Cohuna in northern Victoria.

Continue reading...
title: Former AFL star Nicky Winmar jailed for six months for assault on woman

author: Haroon Siddique Legal affairs correspondent
description:
Course at Donald Trump’s Turnberry resort was painted with words ‘Gaza is not 4 sale’ and clubhouse was sprayed with graffiti

Seven people charged with vandalising Donald Trump’s Turnberry golf course in Scotland have been accused of malicious damage “having a terrorist connection”.

The clubhouse at the five-star Trump Turnberry hotel and resort on the west coast of Scotland was graffitied on 8 March last year and the course was dug up and painted with the words “Gaza is not 4 sale”.

Continue reading...
title: Seven charged with damaging Trump’s Scottish golf course accused of ‘terrorist connection’

author: Steven Morris
description:
A zero-emission compact hydrogen power plant will drive the main stage at Clifton Down in Bristol

When Lorde, Little Simz and Wet Leg stride on to stages in Bristol this weekend, they will not only be entertaining tens of thousands of festivalgoers but taking part in what is being billed as a world-first clean power project.

The two stages at Forwards festival on Clifton Down are being driven almost entirely by green power – a combination of hydrogen and mobile batteries charged with sustainable energy.

Continue reading...
title: ‘No precedent’: Lorde and Little Simz to star at world-first festival run on clean power

author: Aisha Down
description:
Other governments could seek similar concessions, while separate legal action is pending in places ranging from Kenya to the Netherlands

In October 2021, Abrham Meareg’s father, a professor of chemistry in Ethiopia’s northern town of Bahir Dar, was shot at close range and died outside his family home. This was in the middle of the country’s civil war.

For weeks, Facebook’s algorithm had actively promoted posts calling for the academic to be murdered, according to Meareg and Foxglove, a nonprofit organisation supporting Meareg’s lawsuit against the company in Kenya. These posts included photos of his father and his home address.

Continue reading...
title: What could Meta’s US settlement mean around the world – and what now for other claims against firm?

author: Patrick Barkham
description:
Woolston Eyes in Warrington, a dumping ground for canal dredgings, has become best place in UK for black-necked grebe

A dumping ground for dredgings from the Manchester Ship Canal has become the best place in Britain for the rare and beautiful black-necked grebe, hosting 64% of Britain’s breeding population.

Since 2021, Woolston Eyes in Cheshire has been restored, extended and turned into a mosaic of freshwater pools, reedbeds, willow scrub and rough grassland, managed by the RSPB and Woolston Eyes Conservation Group.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Nature thrives when given a chance’: restored Cheshire wetland now a haven for rare grebe

author: Associated Press
description:
President’s directive stalls for a second time about a week before the first postal ballots are due to be sent out

A federal judge on Thursday halted – at least for the moment – attempts to implement Donald Trump’s executive order limiting mail voting.

The president’s directive stalled for a second time about a week before the first mail ballots are due to be sent out for the rapidly approaching midterm elections. In the US district court, Judge Indira Talwani placed a 14-day hold on the government implementing the order in a case that could be headed back to the supreme court, which on Monday overturned an earlier ruling of hers that had blocked Trump’s order from taking effect.
title: Federal judge again halts Trump’s executive order limiting mail voting in midterms

author: Nino Bucci and Henry Belot
description:
Family of two Sydney boys and their parents, who are among 39 Australians identified as missing after flash flooding, ‘worried, but hopeful’

The family of two Sydney boys who went missing with their parents in flash flooding in Nepal say they remain hopeful they will be found safe.

Shylaja Muralitharan, 42, her husband, Chandrasekaran Muralitharan, 47, and their two sons Ashwin, 14 and Aarush, 11, were taking part in a pilgrimage when the flood hit on Wednesday morning.

Continue reading...
title: ‘We just want them to return’: relatives of Australians missing in Nepal floods wait anxiously for news of loved ones

author: Guardian staff and agency
description:
Decision allows manufacturers to begin shipping doses, but confusion remains about insurance coverage

The US Food and Drug Administration approved updated Covid-19 vaccines on Thursday, allowing manufacturers to begin shipping doses to pharmacies and doctors’ offices across the country.

The FDA approved Moderna, Novavax-Sanofi and Pfizer-BioNTech’s updated Covid vaccines, the companies ⁠said on Thursday, ⁠after ​an advisory panel recommended that the shots should target ⁠the dominant XFG variant.

Continue reading...
title: FDA approves updated Covid-19 vaccines for dominant XFG variant
